claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you some questions.

Let's start with the basics:

1. **Do you have any children, and if so, how many children are you inquiring about?** Please provide their names and ages.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi, yes I'm asking about my son Alex. He's 8 years old.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! So you're inquiring about your son Alex, who is 8 years old.

Now I need to ask you a few more questions to determine your eligibility:

**Do you currently live in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great, thank you. 

Next question: **Does Alex live with you?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he doesn't live with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that Alex doesn't live with you.

**Do you contribute financially towards Alex's upkeep?** For example, do you pay for things like food, clothes, pocket money, or contribute to his accommodation costs?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I do help out. I contribute towards things like his clothes and other things he needs.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information.

To help me assess your eligibility more accurately, I need to know: **How much do you contribute towards Alex's upkeep, and how often do you make these contributions?** (For example, weekly, monthly, or as lump sum payments)

This is important because to qualify for Child Benefit when your child lives with someone else, you generally need to contribute at least the same amount as the Child Benefit payment (or the equivalent in kind) towards their upkeep.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I contribute £30 a week towards Alex's needs.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for providing that detail.

One more important question: **Who does Alex currently live with, and is that person claiming Child Benefit for him?** 

This is important because only one person can get Child Benefit for a child at a time.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: He lives with his mum, but she's not claiming Child Benefit for him. Nobody else is getting it for Alex.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for providing all that information. Let me assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex.

Based on what you've told me:
- Alex is 8 years old (under 16)
- You live in the UK
- Alex doesn't live with you - he lives with his mum
- You contribute £30 per week towards Alex's upkeep
- His mum is not claiming Child Benefit, and nobody else is claiming for him

The key factor here is whether your contributions are sufficient. According to the rules, when a child lives with someone else, you can continue to get Child Benefit if you contribute to your child's upkeep by at least the same amount as the Child Benefit payment.

Currently, the weekly Child Benefit rate for one child is approximately £25.60 per week (for the eldest/only child). Since you're contributing £30 per week, which is more than the Child Benefit payment amount, you meet this requirement.

You appear to be eligible for Child Benefit for Alex, as you're making sufficient contributions towards his upkeep and nobody else is claiming for him.
